def-crossing-number-of-link:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be an unoriented link type in $S^3$. Its **crossing number** $c(K)$ is the least element of
$$\{\,n\in\mathbb N:\text{some regular diagram of }K\text{ has exactly }n\text{ crossings}\,\}.$$
def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-:
## Definition

A **2-tangle diagram** is a regular diagram in a disk of two properly embedded tangle arcs and possibly finitely many closed tangle components, with four specified endpoints on the disk boundary; the arcs and circles are disjoint in the represented 3-ball, while their projections may have crossings. A **flyping circle** is a simple closed curve in the projection sphere whose intersection with the diagram consists of exactly three points, exactly one of which is a crossing; the circle is transverse to both branches at that crossing and to the diagram at the other two points. A small annular neighborhood of this circle has two complementary tangle disks. A **flype** fixes the tangle in one disk, interchanges which pair of strands crosses in the annular neighborhood, and turns over the tangle in the other disk: its projected tangle is reflected and all its over-under crossing data are reversed. This turnover is a half-turn in three-dimensional space about an axis in the projection sphere. Component orientations are transported by this motion, and the exterior diagram is fixed. The move with the opposite choice of fixed disk is also allowed; a disk containing no crossings is allowed. A flype whose fixed tangle has no crossings is called an **entire flype**. Diagrams are drawn on the oriented projection sphere; a **sphere planar isotopy** is an orientation-preserving smooth isotopy of that sphere carrying the decorated diagram. A plane diagram is obtained by choosing a point of the sphere outside the projection and deleting it. At each crossing of a link diagram, a **crossing ball** is a small 3-ball in which the overpass lies on the upper hemisphere and the underpass lies on the lower hemisphere, with the rest of the link outside that ball. Replacing all crossing disks by upper hemispheres or by lower hemispheres gives the shifted projection spheres $S_+$ and $S_-$. A **saddle disk** in a crossing ball is a properly embedded disk whose boundary meets each of the two hemispheres in two arcs and whose interior passes across the equatorial crossing disk. For a closed embedded surface transverse to the link and to $S_+$ and $S_-$, each component $C$ of its intersection with either shifted sphere has a **bubble word**: read once around $C$, recording $P$ each time it crosses the link and $S$ each time it passes through a crossing ball along a saddle disk. The surface is in **bubble standard position** if every such word is nonempty and no word records the same crossing ball more than once. A **Conway sphere** is an embedded sphere meeting the link transversely in four points; it is in crossing-ball standard position when its intersection with the crossing balls consists of saddle disks and its shifted-sphere intersection curves satisfy the bubble-standard conditions.

The turnover convention is the one in Kindred's Definition 2.9 and Figure 1. In particular, an entire flype permits viewing the whole diagram from the opposite side of the sphere, as in his Definition 2.11. Closed components inside a tangle disk are carried along with its arcs.
def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram:
## Definition

A regular link diagram is **connected** when its underlying projection graph is connected. It is **alternating** when successive crossing visits along each component switch between overpasses and underpasses. It is **reduced** when no complementary region of the projection sphere has a crossing more than once on its boundary. A connected alternating diagram that is reduced is a **reduced alternating link diagram**.
def-split-link:
## Definition

An oriented link $L\subset S^3$ is **split** if a smoothly embedded sphere $S\subset S^3\setminus L$ has link points in both components of $S^3\setminus S$; otherwise $L$ is **nonsplit**.
def-tait-graph-of-a-link-diagram:
## Definition

For a link projection on $S^2$, a **checkerboard coloring** assigns one of two colors to each complementary region so that regions sharing an edge have different colors. Given such a coloring, the **black Tait graph** has one vertex for each black region and one edge for each crossing joining the two opposite black sectors at that crossing. The **white Tait graph** is defined by interchanging black and white. Loops and parallel edges are allowed.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c:
## Statement

Let $P\subset S^2$ be the finite connected 4-valent graph underlying a regular link projection. Its complementary regions have exactly two colorings with two colors such that regions sharing an edge have different colors.
lem-disconnected-projection-components-s:
## Statement

Let $P\subset S^2$ be the finite projection graph of a regular link diagram. If $P$ is disconnected, there is a simple closed curve $\gamma\subset S^2\setminus P$ such that $P$ has points on both sides of $\gamma$.
lem-connected-projection-has-connected-t:
## Statement

For a connected regular link projection on $S^2$ with at least one crossing and either checkerboard coloring, both Tait graphs are connected.
lem-disconnected-link-diagram-represents:
## Statement

If the underlying projection of a regular link diagram on $S^2$ is disconnected, then the represented link is split.
lem-definite-normal-pairing-forces-nonsp:
## Statement

Let $F\subset S^3$ be a compact connected smoothly embedded surface with nonempty boundary $L$, supplied with a finite disk-and-band presentation. The surface may be nonorientable. A normal transfer $\tau c$ of an oriented rational multicurve $c$ in the interior of $F$ is its total inverse image in the boundary of a sufficiently small normal interval neighborhood of $F$, oriented by projection onto $c$. Suppose a quadratic form $q$ on $H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$ is positive definite or negative definite and satisfies $q([c])=\operatorname{lk}(c,\tau c)$ for every such rational multicurve. Then $L$ is nonsplit. Definiteness on the zero vector space is allowed.
lem-connected-diagram-bracket-span-bound:
## Statement

For a connected regular link diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings, the Laurent-polynomial span of its Kauffman bracket is at most $4c$. If $D$ is reduced and alternating, then changing any one crossing from the all-$A$ state or the all-$B$ state merges two distinct state circles, both extreme coefficients are nonzero, and the bracket span is exactly $4c$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.
lem-alternating-checkerboard-normal-pair:
## Statement

Let $D$ be a connected alternating regular link diagram on an oriented projection sphere. Choose either checkerboard color. Put a disk in each region of that color and join the opposite colored sectors at every crossing by a half-twisted band, with the twist chosen so that the boundary follows the over-under diagram. After rounding corners these disks and bands form a compact connected embedded spanning surface $F$ for the represented link. If $D$ has crossings, let $G$ be the corresponding Tait graph and orient its edges arbitrarily. Under the retraction of $F$ onto $G$, write a rational homology class as the unique graph cycle $a=\sum_{e\in E(G)}a_e e$. There is a single sign $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ such that
$$q(a)=\epsilon\sum_{e\in E(G)}a_e^2=\operatorname{lk}(c,\tau c)$$
for every oriented rational multicurve $c$ representing $a$, where $\tau c$ is its normal transfer. Thus $q$ is positive definite or negative definite on $H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$. For a crossingless connected diagram, use either spanning disk and the zero-dimensional definite form.
lem-connected-alternating-link-is-nonspl:
## Statement

If a regular link diagram on $S^2$ is connected and alternating, then the represented link is nonsplit.
thm-reduced-alternating-diagram-minimize:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ of an oriented link $L$ realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link: $c(D)=c(L)$.
thm-tait-flyping-theorem:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Any two connected reduced alternating diagrams on the oriented projection sphere that represent the same oriented link type are related by a finite sequence of sphere planar isotopies and flypes. Composite links are included; the diagrams are required to be connected, and a plane drawing is interpreted as a punctured projection sphere.
lem-alternating-state-adequacy-and-jones:
## Statement

Assume full AC and let $D$ be a connected reduced alternating diagram with $c$ crossings. At every crossing, changing one smoothing from the all-$A$ state or from the all-$B$ state merges two distinct state circles; these are A- and B-adequacy. The Kauffman bracket has $A$-span $4c$. If $D$ represents a knot $K$, then the library Jones polynomial has $t$-span $c$, and every $c'$-crossing diagram of $K$ has $t$-span at most $c'$ under the convention $t=A^{-4}$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.
cor-jones-span-detects-crossing-number-f:
## Statement

Assume full AC. If $D$ is a connected reduced alternating diagram of a knot $K$, then the library Jones polynomial has $t$-span exactly $c(K)=c(D)$, in the convention $t=A^{-4}$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.
